investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-29T23:16–23:24Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the production cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the remote agent pod because 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner received no evidence — leaving all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes in the production-api cluster. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (resource quota exhausted or limit reached), and the remaining 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable. As a result, the pod remained Unschedulable for 136–142 seconds until the eval timeout fired, no VM was ever started, and the runner could not collect any of the required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) mandated by the expected-output contract at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256.

possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource quota exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: the 2 nodes that support peer-pod VMs have reached their maximum concurrent VM allocation, leaving no capacity for a new pod. This is the most directly supported cause given the scheduler message 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' (failed-check.message).

Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod specifies a node selector or affinity rule that only matches the 2 kata-capable nodes, and those 2 nodes are already at capacity. If the affinity rules were broadened or more kata-capable nodes were available, scheduling would succeed.

Cluster-level resource pressure or node scaling lag: the production cluster may not have auto-scaled to add additional kata-capable nodes in time, or auto-scaling is not configured for this node pool, leaving the 2 kata nodes as the only eligible targets.

Concurrent remote agent workloads consuming all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: other running pods or eval runs may have consumed all available VM slots on the 2 eligible nodes before this eval's pod was submitted.

Misconfigured or stale resource limit on kata.peerpods.io/vm: the extended resource limit advertised by the 2 nodes may be set too low relative to actual hardware capacity, causing premature exhaustion.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Kata Peer-Pods VM Capacity Exhausted on Production Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-29T23:19–23:24Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the production cluster's 6 nodes cannot schedule new kata.peerpods.io/vm pods because 2 nodes report insufficient kata peer-pod VM quota and 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never returned an agent, and therefore no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written — causing the expected-output contract to fail with all four required fields missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available production nodes. Two nodes that support the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource class reported insufficient capacity (quota or slot exhaustion), and the remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector constraints. Preemption was also unavailable. The pod remained Unschedulable for ~142 seconds before the eval timed out. Because the pod never started, the agent was never created, and the eval runner never reached the state-polling logic that would produce the required evidence fields. This is an infrastructure-layer failure in the production Kubernetes cluster's kata peer-pods VM pool, not a code defect in the eval runner or its contracts.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-29T23:16–23:24Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the production cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the remote agent pod because 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner received no evidence — leaving all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes in the production-api cluster. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (resource quota exhausted or limit reached), and the remaining 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable. As a result, the pod remained Unschedulable for 136–142 seconds until the eval timeout fired, no VM was ever started, and the runner could not collect any of the required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) mandated by the expected-output contract at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-29T23:19–23:24Z because newly requested pods could not be scheduled: the Kubernetes cluster reported 2 nodes with insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes that did not match the pod's node affinity/selector, leaving 0 of 6 nodes available. Because no agent pod was ever scheduled, the eval runner never received any response payload, causing all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) to be absent and the expected-output contract assertion on message containing "hello from aura" to go unverified.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the two nodes that carry that resource. The remaining four nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With no schedulable node available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out unscheduled (~136–142 s), preventing the eval from reaching the agent runtime and producing any evidence. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the production-api remote-agent swarm cluster; it is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure constraint, but no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a user-facing outage.
